paper_title: Iron-Catalyzed Aerobic Oxidation of Alcohols: Lower Cost and Improved Selectivity

questions.question: In this paper, what compound does the label '1a' refer to (give the molecular formula/name exactly as shown in the article)?
What is the structure/name of the product labeled '2a' formed from oxidation of 1a (provide the exact representation used in the paper)?
For the 100 mmol-scale aerobic oxidation of 1a performed with a slow flow of air, what catalyst loadings, solvent, air flow rate, temperature and reaction time were used?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Fe(NO3)3·9H2O 5 mol%, 4‑OH‑TEMPO 10 mol%, NaCl 10 mol%; solvent DCE; air flow 30 mL/min; 25 °C; 15.5 h.

questions.question: According to Table 2 in the article, which solvent gave the higher yield for conversion of 1a to 2a — dichloromethane (DCM) or toluene — and what yields are reported for each?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Toluene gave the higher yield: DCM 65% vs toluene 77% (reported yields in Table 2).

questions.question: What yield(s) of aldehyde 2a were obtained from the 100 mmol-scale oxidation of 1a with a slow flow of air (report both NMR and isolated yields as given)?
